title: Differential-Matching Prefetcher for Indirect Memory Access
problem: Indirect memory access patterns, where values from one array generate addresses for another, create irregular data accesses with poor temporal and spatial locality that conventional prefetchers cannot capture. Nested multi-level patterns further disrupted by branch mispredictions make them extremely difficult to prefetch effectively.
motivation: Indirect memory access is a critical bottleneck for modern CPUs in graph analysis and sparse linear algebra applications, significantly limiting performance and energy efficiency.
method: DMP predicts indirect memory accesses by watching the pattern of which array positions you access and what values those positions contain, then using those values as addresses for the next memory access. It detects four pattern types: one-to-one mappings, ranges, nested chains through multiple array layers, and branching paths. The system adjusts prefetch depth based on how many cache misses it prevents, using only 0.9 kilobytes of storage.
key_novelty: Differential matching identifies patterns in indirect memory accesses by correlating which array positions are accessed with the values stored there, enabling detection of patterns nested across multiple array levels.
contributions: Differential-Matching Prefetcher (DMP) architecture targeting single, range, multi-level, and multi-way indirect memory access patterns
Differential matching technique to identify indirect patterns correlated with index streams
Dynamic prefetching degree adaptation mechanism for maintaining coverage on irregular workloads
Low-cost implementation with only 0.9KB storage overhead, enabling practical CPU integration

metrics.speedup: 1.8× average (up to 5.6×) vs. state-of-the-art hardware prefetchers; 1.2× (up to 2.3×) vs. Prodigy

primary_theme: Hardware prefetching for indirect memory access patterns
